quote: we have a a solar system now, a 10 kilowatt hour solar system that we got from a company called Namaste, and they no longer service our ZIP code.
stewart_read: Customer discloses an existing solar system — the orphaned_flow trigger — but the rep never runs the ownership/lease or DQ-company checklist against it.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the system's origin (Namaste, not Sunrun/Pink Solar) as automatically clear of the DQ list, making the skip low-risk in this instance.
coaching_implication: Ask explicitly: own or lease, and is it currently working — even when the story sounds clean, the gate exists for a reason.

quote: we are buying electricity again... So wanna add a few more panels.
stewart_read: EV ownership plus a hot tub driving up usage is exactly the profile that makes an expansion sale easier — strong qualified enthusiasm.
coaching_implication: Rep should reflect this back explicitly ('so the EV and hot tub are what's pushing you over') to reinforce the customer's own reason to expand — she let it pass without anchoring it.

stewart_read: Bill figure captured cleanly but never flipped or reflected back — rep says only 'Okay' and moves straight to the next script item.
alternative_hypothesis: Customer explicitly said this isn't a cost-payback conversation ('we're not looking at this from a cost payback type situation'), so a bill-pain flip may genuinely not fit this profile — he's motivated by capacity/backup, not bill pain.
coaching_implication: Given the customer's own framing, the flip target should shift from bill pain to capacity/backup pain — rep could have anchored on 'so the EV and hot tub already outpaced what your system covers' instead of bill dollars.

quote: We had to Yeave our roof replaced at one point, and I was very happy to not have to have the panels removed and then put it back out.
stewart_read: Customer raises panel removal/roof-replacement history and considering roof-mount vs ground-mount for new panels — rep responds with lift-and-replace capability but does not probe whether a near-term roof project is coming up now.
alternative_hypothesis: This was framed as a past event, not a planned future roof job, so the standard roof_replacement_planned bridge may not apply as strongly here.
coaching_implication: Even referencing past experience, worth a quick check: 'is your garage roof due for replacement soon, since you mentioned putting panels there?' to surface a live roofing opportunity.

quote: Do you have anything on Thursday, the thirtieth?
stewart_read: Wife Jeanette was identified as co-owner on title but never explicitly confirmed as attending the appointment — the appointment was scheduled around the customer's and his wife's shared availability by inference only.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep did ask 'do mornings or afternoons work best for you and your wife' at 09:17, which implicitly includes her — this may be adequate inclusion rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: Get an explicit confirmation that Jeanette will be on the call, not just inferred from a shared-availability question.

quote: Yes. You said it? Okay. Perfect.
stewart_read: Button-up covers time block and text follow-up but never runs the explicit 'is that fair?' handshake or the no-driving/sit-down-at-computer instruction.
coaching_implication: Add the explicit computer/no-driving line and the fairness check — both are tied to no-show rate per schema.
